misconceptions.description: Designing slide content for the wrong audience or an unstated purpose
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes the deck for peers when the stated audience is a hiring panel, or never names the purpose
misconceptions.feedback: Write one sentence naming who the audience is and the single decision they should make, then check every slide against it.

misconceptions.description: Believing one finished deck transfers unchanged to any audience or time limit
misconceptions.trigger: learner reuses a 12-minute classroom deck for a 3-minute recruiter pitch without cutting
misconceptions.feedback: Re-derive scope from the new constraint: a 3-minute slot means roughly 3 to 4 slides, not the full 12.

misconceptions.description: Treating visual polish as proof the deck fits its audience and purpose
misconceptions.trigger: learner points to animations and a theme but cannot say what the audience needs to do
misconceptions.feedback: Audience fit comes first: name the takeaway, then add polish only where it helps that takeaway land.
